reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, a stated part of wound repair.
expectation: The cells will clear debris from the wound.

alternatives.reason: The picture also suggests signals act on the nearby vessel.

effect: The wound is cleared of debris, leaving the supporting layer and surface closure to address.
reaction: The result matched the picture and made the first repair step clear.
reason: The repair signals are shown acting on the nearby capillary, suggesting a role in supplying the healing wound.
expectation: The signals will prompt the capillary to grow toward the wound.

effect: The signals prompted a capillary branch to grow toward the wound; it remains connected to the circulation.
reaction: The result matched the picture, though its contribution to repair is not yet explained.
reason: Fibroblasts build connective tissue, and the matrix nutrients provide raw materials for that work.
expectation: The fibroblasts will produce material for the wound’s supporting layer.

effect: The fibroblasts used the nutrients to make collagen-containing connective tissue, providing material for the wound’s support.
reaction: The result made the fibroblasts’ role clear.
reason: The epidermal edge cells need nutrients to grow across and close the surface.
expectation: The cells will form new surface tissue for the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface sheet that can close the wound.
reaction: The result clearly shows how the surface is repaired.
reason: The cleaned wound needs the new connective tissue for support.
expectation: The new connective tissue will support the damaged area.

effect: The wound first needed the capillary sprout; the resulting healing skin has slots for the new surface and support.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the required order, though I had expected to add the connective tissue directly.
reason: The new connective tissue fits the support slot in the healing skin.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot.

effect: The connective tissue fills the support slot, and the result explains that the new tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin.
reaction: The explanation makes the support's role and its limits clear.
reason: The new surface matches the remaining surface slot.
expectation: The new epidermal sheet will fill the surface slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface closed the gap and completed the wound-support goal; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: The distinction between closure and deeper strengthening is clear.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, so they should act on the healed wound's remaining clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The enzymes cleared the temporary clot, completing the goals. The remaining scar is still maturing as its collagen changes.
reaction: The distinction between a closed wound and a fully mature repair was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding connective tissue and the new surface made their different roles in supporting and closing the wound clear. The explanation that young tissue is still weaker also added useful context.

leastWorthwhile.text: The capillary sprout was required before adding support, but its contribution to healing was not explained when it appeared. The required order was initially unclear.

surprise.text: I expected to add connective tissue directly to the cleaned wound; compatibility feedback instead combined it with the capillary sprout and revealed the surface and support slots.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the capillary sprout before adding connective tissue felt somewhat arbitrary because the result did not explain why that order mattered.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it offered similarly clear links between cellular work and the body's recovery, though I would hope for more explanation where a required order is not obvious.
